instructions.question: What overall sentiment does the tweet's author express, judging by a clear attitude, mood or evaluation rather than the topic alone?
instructions.rule: Use positive or negative when the author's own feeling is plain, even if mild. Public invitations to come enjoy or join an event, giveaways, and celebrated milestones or records are positive, but plain scores, leads, game results, ticket sales, listings and asking a friend to come along are neutral. Wry jokes about one's own situation, corrections, team or injury news, and opinions on politics, religion or sport without insults are neutral. Personal setbacks (can't make it, can't go), sarcastic digs, and news of violence, deaths or scandal are negative.

neutral.what: Facts, questions, scores, listings, ticket sales, logistics, sports commentary, debating replies, corrections, wry remarks without real complaint.
examples: Trayce Thompson's 2-run double gives the White Sox a 5-4 lead in the 7th.
OMG. Who wants to go see Duelo with me this Friday!?
Wantin to go out tonite....but no one to go out with so i guess i'll be on netflix  tonite
@user You do realize that the 1st Amendment doesn't just apply to Christians, right?
neutral.cues: lead, win, round, pm me, tickets, who wants to, I guess, right?, may, should
neutral.not_for: Open gushing is positive; insults, sadness, :(, #fml or can't-make-it regrets are negative.

positive.what: Enthusiasm, love, praise, eager wanting, condolences, inviting promos, giveaways, or celebrated milestones.
examples: Come enjoy Splash Dance with Robbie Riviera this Thursday @user
8th strikeout of the afternoon for David Price's 100th career win!
noel fielding may be one of the greatest people alive.
I want IHOP tomorrow morning
positive.cues: come enjoy, join us, invite your friends, chance to win, can't wait, love, best, rest in peace, <3
positive.not_for: Plain game results, leads, 'who wants to go with me?' and plain plans are neutral.

negative.what: Clear complaint, disappointment, sadness, boredom, personal setback, insult, mockery or sarcasm, or news of violence or scandal.
examples: Dream High 2 sucks compared to the 1st one.
Just remembered I'm taking the PSSAs tomorrow. #Fml
I wanna go to the studio with Ulysses n them tomorrow,but i cant. #BARS
The best way to find Malaysia Airlines Flight MH370 may be with Michelle Obama's arms.
negative.cues: sucks, disappointed, #fml, #boring, :(, but I can't, sorry I can't make it, hate, wtf, shot dead
negative.not_for: Wry self-jokes, mild critique of athletes and team injury news are neutral.
